methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $70M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Neustark is a Series B climate and energy company that has raised $70M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private comparables—KoBold Metals (Series C, $3.0B), Electric Hydrogen (Series C, $1.0B), and Amogy (Series C, $700M)—alongside a broader comp set of nine private firms and one public entity (LNZA).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier, yields $133M. Peer-median analysis across the three identified comparables produces a $1.0B implied valuation, with observed range of $700M to $3.0B. The stage gap between Neustark (Series B) and the median peer set (Series C) introduces upward bias in the peer method; conversely, the capital-raised proxy understates expected value at maturity.

Triangulation across both methods supports a valuation range of $113M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $566M. Key uncertainties center on the appropriate stage-discount adjustment relative to Series C peers and whether near-term funding trajectory and market conditions support the peer median. The wide dispersion ($113M–$1.1B) reflects both methodological sensitivity and fundamental heterogeneity within the climate-tech sector.
